intelligence.enrichment: During adolescence, visible body changes can include increased height, changes in body structure, weight gain, greater strength, voice changes, acne, and new hair in parts of the body. The timing, nature, and extent of these changes vary among individuals and this variation is normal. adolescent growth -> visible physical changes; individual variation -> different timing and extent of changes The learner classifies visible changes such as height, body structure, voice, pimples, and body hair as normal adolescent changes while preserving individual variation. Adolescent change means the same obvious body changes happen to every student in the same grade.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: Adolescence. The student must decide: Decide whether common visible changes such as increased height, broader shoulders, wider chest, pimples, hoarse voice, or new body hair are normal adolescent changes rather than identical changes for every person. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
